proof_summary: The truncated Catalan sum is rewritten as \(U(n,n(m+2))=[x^n]g(x)(1+x)^{n(m+2)}\), where \(g(x)=(1-x)^2(1+x)/(1-x^3)\) has period-three coefficients.  Expanding \((1+x)^p=1+x^p+p\Phi_p(x)\), one shows \(1+x+x^2\mid\Phi_p\), so \(g\Phi_p^t\) is anti-palindromic; pairing its coefficients makes the relevant binomial differences highly \(p\)-divisible, and combined valuation estimates (with the \(t=1,2\) terms vanishing and binomial/Mahler interpolation handling integer exponents) yield the required cubic gain at every prime-power step.
